findings.text: follow-on: the goal's phrase "without one of FINDING_SEVERITIES" has two halves — absent and outside the vocabulary — and only the absent half is asserted; test_a_record_with_an_unmarked_finding_is_refused_at_the_write feeds only severities the store dropped, and test_a_record_whose_findings_all_state_a_severity_is_not_refused feeds only the two declared values, so a regression that changed `_severity_stated` to accept any non-null severity (reckon/crew/reports.py:1170) would leave every case green while the written-directly `minor`/`moderate`/`low` records the plan names stayed unread; the remedy is one case storing a finding whose severity is outside FINDING_SEVERITIES and asserting it is refused.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against base 84fd7ff4f; a8b598af1 adds the check to reckon/crew/reports.py and the falsifier, 721907273 adds the evidence fragment, nothing outside the declared paths.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names a base arm, a four-case falsifier in a new tests/test_an_unmarked_finding_is_refused_at_write.py built from a record written through the production store, a negative control removing the check, and both arms over the new test plus every existing test file that calls audit_manifest; the manifest records base 2 failed/489 passed and head 1 failed/490 passed with no added failure id, and I re-ran the new file at head (4 passed) and at base with the file placed in the tree (1 failed/3 passed, the unmarked case) to confirm both.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that audit_manifest reports a review run whose stored record carries any finding without one of FINDING_SEVERITIES, naming each such finding's file and line; reckon/crew/reports.py:1439 adds `_unmarked_finding_severity_findings(node)` to audit_manifest, gated on the node's role being the review role (reckon/crew/reports.py:1163 `_node_is_a_reviewer`), and I confirmed against this run's own live pointer that a review dispatch declares exactly the two store record paths the check reads.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records both suite arms as JSON with completed true and literal absolute-path commands, the negative-control log, and the added-failure derivation, all of which I recomputed independently.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the manifest's declared scope (reckon/crew/reports.py, tests/test_an_unmarked_finding_is_refused_at_write.py, docs/evidence/fragments/scoring-should-stop-a-promotion/an-unmarked-finding-is-refused-at-write.html); `git diff --stat 84fd7ff4f 721907273` lists exactly those three paths.

justifications.durability: tests/test_an_unmarked_finding_is_refused_at_write.py:124 reddens when the check call is removed (I reinstated that mutation and got EXIT=1), but the goal's "outside the vocabulary" half is unasserted at tests/test_an_unmarked_finding_is_refused_at_write.py:146.
justifications.evidence: tests/test_an_unmarked_finding_is_refused_at_write.py:112 asserts the refusal and gate/base-gate.log records it failing at 84fd7ff4f while gate/head-gate.log records it passing at a8b598af1, both ended EXIT=1 with revision-named headers I re-ran to confirm.
justifications.fit: reckon/crew/reports.py:1135 follows the surrounding finding-producer idiom and the new test file name describes the behaviour, adding no plan or ticket identifier; ruff check over both changed Python paths reports the same two pre-existing findings as the base.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/reports.py:1147 `_unmarked_finding_severity_findings` reads the declared store record through `review_module.stored_record` and reports every finding whose severity is absent or outside FINDING_SEVERITIES, exactly as the goal states.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in `git diff 84fd7ff4f 721907273` sits inside the two declared source paths and the one evidence fragment, with no change to the parser the goal says stays unchanged.
